data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is a confound of one-repository, one-author, one-week arbitrariness: the distribution (compile.py 1/9 vs. 4/4 to 6/7 elsewhere) reflects where the author happened to install shown-to-fail-first tests as guards, not any general condition under which tests constrain rather than describe their subjects.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the same distribution replicated across multiple independent authors or repositories, the confound explanation would weaken.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py mutations were systematically different in kind (e.g., all outside guard scope) rather than differing only in installation order, the distribution would not be arbitrary.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 losses are shown to be caused by guard coverage rather than installation ritual, the confound claim would be overturned.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a written policy required shown-to-fail-first installation uniformly and the distribution still showed 1/9 for compile.py, the arbitrariness mechanism would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a single-author, single-week project, the decision to install a test as shown-to-fail-first is made ad hoc per module. Modules where the author happened to write a guard and demonstrate its failure before mutation acceptance become constrained (4/4 to 6/7 losses); modules where the author did not perform this ritual (compile.py) remain merely described (1/9 loss). The condition is therefore not a property of tests or subjects but of the author's installation order: a test constrains its subject when the author has ritually installed it as a fail-first authority, and this ritual is arbitrary and unevenly applied.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
